title: ATSB: R44 collided with tree during low-level spraying over complex terrain
summary: The Riverina Helicopters-operated Robinson R44 Raven II was being used for noxious weed spraying, the Australian Transport Safety Bureau (ATSB) said.
body_markdown:
A Robinson R44 helicopter collided with a tree during low-level spraying over complex terrain near Young, New South Wales, an Australian Transport Safety Bureau (ATSB) final report details.


The Riverina Helicopters-operated Robinson R44 Raven II was being used for noxious weed spraying at a property near Boorowa, about 50 kilometers south-east of Young on Dec. 4, 2024.


Before the first spraying flight, the operator’s Griffith base manager accompanied the pilot to survey the target area in the helicopter, and returned about five minutes later.


The pilot then conducted 10 spraying flights of roughly 10 minutes each, returning to the load site between flights to replenish with herbicide and fuel.


During the 11th spray flight, while flying low over steep terrain, the helicopter struck a dead tree, and then collided with terrain. The helicopter slid across sloping terrain before entering a gully, and the pilot was fatally injured.


“Based on a comprehensive analysis of the evidence available to the ATSB, no single factor contributing to the collision with the tree could be determined with any reasonable degree of certainty,” ATSB chief commissioner Angus Mitchell said.


Among potential contributing factors discussed in the report, it was hypothesized the pilot may not have seen the tree, which was set against high terrain and dead grass, in time to avoid a collision.


“ATSB examination of the accident site concluded the collision with the tree dislodged the stabilizer assembly and tail rotor system,” Mitchell continued.


“While some abnormalities were found during examination and testing of components recovered from the accident site, none were concluded likely to have contributed to the accident, and there was also no evidence of any flight control or mechanical abnormality.”


However, the report notes the possibility of an intermittent issue, or unknown emergency with the helicopter, could not be completely discounted.


“We do know that low-level flight over complex terrain, within the obstacle environment, brings several significant complexities to an operation,” Mitchell concluded.


“One such complexity is the significantly reduced time available to diagnose and respond to issues with the helicopter.


“Another is not seeing obstructions in an area too complex to remember every detail.”


**Read the final report:**[Collision with terrain involving Robinson R44 II, VH-XIX, 50 km east of Young Airport, New South Wales, on 4 December 2024](https://www.atsb.gov.au/node/11172)


*This press release was prepared and distributed by the Australian Transport Safety Bureau.*
